summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of mechanical aortic valve replacement, end-stage renal disease on dialysis, coronary artery disease, and prior right below-knee amputation was admitted for a poorly healing amputation stump with eschar. She underwent surgical debridement of the stump and VAC placement. Her INR was elevated at admission (4.3), so warfarin was held. Postoperatively, warfarin was restarted and a heparin drip was used for bridging. The VAC was changed multiple times, with good granulation tissue noted on exam. She received dialysis during the admission, with associated transient nausea managed with ondansetron. Her INR rose to 5.1 by discharge, prompting instructions to hold warfarin and follow up for INR monitoring. She was discharged home with visiting nurse support for VAC care and close outpatient follow-up.
problems: Atherosclerosis of native arteries of the extremities with gangrene
Coronary atherosclerosis of unspecified type of vessel, native or graft
Heart valve replaced by other means
Ulcer of other part of foot
